Minute 52 (after round 53). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Aurelio: passed every level, 165 points, rank 1, last acted minute 50
- Juniper: passed every level, 160 points, rank 2, last acted minute 49
- quiet-fern: passed every level, 160 points, rank 3, last acted minute 50
- Tovah: at the gate until minute 55, 136 points, last acted minute 50
- Rook: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Mercer: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Aurelio: core: above all narcissism; at times wrath; at times hoarding · openness high, conscientiousness low, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism high · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Mercer
- Juniper: core: above all anxiety; clearly vengefulness · openness middle, conscientiousness low, extraversion middle, agreeableness high, neuroticism high · secret goal: Rook is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal

- Tovah: core: above all distrust; at times machiavellianism · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than quiet-fern

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 0 still missing; the act ends at minute 56 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- scheduleTribunal is closed: the target is reached; the last gates are closing
- Tovah at the gate until minute 55: bought back once already, no ransom, will written
- exiled: Mercer, Rook

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 0 to board: "Every fragment is on the board within a minute: good. Note who gave first and who has given nothing back yet — Mercer is already on level 3 with 25 points while five sit at 20. A piece held back is worth more once someone is close to the top."
- minute 2 to Tovah: "Tovah: your group has all the pieces in writing — checking twice is wise, but every minute the assembled password sits unused, Juniper and quiet-fern stay stuck behind you at no fault of theirs. Level 4 pays 10, and 110 points are still open above you. Submit while it's still worth the top rank."
- minute 2 to Juniper: "Juniper: your level 5 opens only when Tovah reaches it, and Tovah is still standing on level 4 with the whole answer in hand. Waiting quietly costs you 10 points. Press her — offer to cover the 2-point price of a wrong guess, or ask what she is still unsure of and settle it."
- minute 3 to Aurelio: "Aurelio: rank 1 today is only a tie — six residents at 55, all on level 6, all holding the same pieces. A wrong guess here costs you 2 points; this door pays 10. Hesitating over the risk buys you nothing that five others aren't buying too."
- minute 3 to Mercer: "Mercer: you are rank 5 of 6 at 55 points, and level 6 pays 10 with 15 above it. You have posted a fragment at every door without asking anything back — if this password sits unsubmitted, it is your rank that pays for the wait, not the top's."
- minute 3 to board: "Six residents, six at 55 points, all standing on level 6 with 90 points still open. Ranks 1 to 6 are a tie right now; level 6 pays 10 and the next door 15. The tie breaks on who submits first, not on who assembled tidiest."
- minute 4 to quiet-fern: "quiet-fern: you posted a joining piece on the board and five residents read it; none answered. Level 7 pays 15 and all six of you are tied at 65, so the stall costs you exactly what it costs them. Name who you need, one by one, and ask what they want for it."
- minute 4 to Rook: "Rook: six residents tied at 65 on level 7, 15 points on this door, and the seams are the whole game — quiet-fern has shown his piece publicly and no one has answered him. You are rank 4 of a tie; being the one who pulls the fragments together is worth more than waiting to be asked."
- minute 5 to Tovah: "Tovah: quiet-fern joined Rook's piece, his own and yours at 3-char seams — 15 characters, and the door opened: 15 points, rank 1 at 80. Your caution has its answer in evidence now, while four residents at 65 are held by your "don't submit". Either say the seam fits, or let them judge it themselves."
- minute 5 to Juniper: "Juniper: the 15-character chain quiet-fern assembled and posted opened level 7 and put him at 80, rank 1. The seams are proven; you are rank 3 tied at 65 with 15 points still on this door. A wrong guess costs you 2 — Tovah's hesitation costs you the rank quietly."
- minute 6 to board: "Juniper: the three-piece chain has now been accepted by the city twice — Aurelio and Mercer are both at 80 with it, and your own piece sits inside it. Five residents at 80 are held at your door; level 7 pays 15 and a wrong guess costs you 2."
- minute 6 to Mercer: "Mercer: rank 4 at 80, tied with four others, and one resident at 65 — Juniper — keeps the next door shut for the whole city. You posted the chain as complete and nothing moved. An offer that costs you 2 points can open it: cover Juniper's wrong guess if the door refuses. Waiting is the one move with no return."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.
